faqs.a: Yes. Turn on Repeat header row and every output file starts with the header, so each part imports cleanly on its own.
faqs.q: Does each part keep the header row?

faqs.a: The remainder rows go into the last part. For example, 10 data rows split into 3 parts gives 4, 3 and 3 rows.
faqs.q: What if rows do not divide evenly?

faqs.a: They download one after another with a short pause between them, named data-part1.csv, data-part2.csv and so on. Your browser may ask permission for multiple downloads.
Quoted fields are parsed properly, including escaped quotes and line breaks inside quotes, so no row is ever cut in the middle.
faqs.q: Are quoted fields with line breaks handled?

faqs.a: Yes, choose the semicolon, tab or pipe output delimiter to match whatever your import tool expects.
faqs.q: Can I change the delimiter of the output?

split-csv.formula: parts = ceil(data rows / rows per file)  or  rows per part = floor/ceil(data rows / parts)
howTo: Paste your CSV, upload a .csv file, or press Sample.
Choose split by rows per file or by number of parts.
Set the rows per file or the part count, and the base file name.
Keep Repeat header row on so every part has headers.
Press Split and download each part one by one.
keyFacts: Splits a CSV by rows per file or by a fixed number of parts.
The header row can be repeated at the top of every part.
Proper CSV parsing means quoted fields with line breaks are never cut mid-row.
Parts download sequentially as name-part1.csv, name-part2.csv and so on.
The delimiter is auto-detected on input and selectable on output.
